classification_signals: Title: 'Physiological effects in humans induced by the visual stimulation of room interiors with different wood quantities' suggests an experimental design.
Abstract: Describes 'measurements' of 'pulse rate, blood pressure, and brain activity' in 'actual-size model rooms' with varying 'wood ratios' (0%, 45%, 90%), and 'subjective evaluation'.

Methodology: 'Materials and methods' section details experimental setup, subject recruitment (15 male students), controlled ambient conditions, continuous physiological measurements (Finapress, NIRS), and subjective questionnaires.
Results: 'Results and discussion' section presents quantitative data, time-series graphs (Figs. 6-9), and statistical analyses (ANOVA, t-tests) with p-values.
Conclusion: Summarizes findings based on the experimental data.
title: Physiological effects in humans induced by the visual stimulation of room interiors with different wood quantities
authors: Yuko Tsunetsugu, Yoshifumi Miyazaki, Hiroshi Sato, 2007

minimum_safe_summary: This empirical study investigated the physiological and subjective effects of different wood quantities (0%, 45%, 90%) in room interiors on human subjects. Key findings indicate that a 45% wood ratio tended to be rated as most comfortable and restful, causing a significant decrease in diastolic blood pressure and an increase in pulse rate. A 90% wood ratio initially led to significant decreases in both systolic and diastolic blood pressure but was associated with a rapid decrease in brain activity and an increase in pulse rate towards the end of exposure, suggesting fatigue. The 0% wood room showed minimal physiological changes but was rated less natural and restful. Limitations include the need for further research into underlying physiological mechanisms and individual differences.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Exposure to natural environments or elements (like wood) can reduce physiological stress responses.
Humans have an innate tendency to connect with nature, leading to positive physiological and psychological responses when exposed to natural elements.

mechanism_chain.description: Visual stimulation of wood-rich interiors is perceived as natural and comforting, leading to a shift in autonomic nervous system activity towards relaxation, which manifests as reduced physiological stress indicators.
